title: Data Analyst
blurb: Data analyst postings screen hard for query and visualization tools first, then for proof you turned analysis into a business decision. Recruiters search ATS databases for the exact tool names, so "SQL" and "Tableau" need to appear verbatim.
bullets: Built a Tableau KPI dashboard used by 40+ managers weekly, replacing 6 manual Excel reports and saving 12 hours a week.
Wrote SQL cohort analysis that found a 22% Day-30 churn spike tied to one onboarding step; the fix cut churn 9 points.
Automated a daily ETL pipeline in dbt and Snowflake, cutting report latency from 3 days to 4 hours.
mistakes: Listing tools with no bullet showing what you did with them.
Describing queries instead of the decision they changed.
Leaving out data volume (rows, users, dollars) that signals scale.

title: Data Scientist
blurb: Data science screens look for modeling depth, the stack you used, and evidence that a model shipped and moved a metric. A list of algorithms without outcomes reads as academic.
certs: Master's degree in a quantitative field
bullets: Shipped a gradient-boosted churn model (AUC 0.86) that targeted retention offers and saved $1.2M ARR in year one.
Designed and analyzed 30+ A/B tests with CUPED variance reduction, cutting required sample sizes 35%.
Built an NLP ticket classifier in PyTorch that auto-routed 60% of support volume.
mistakes: Naming algorithms without the business result.
Omitting how the model was deployed or used.
Burying Python and SQL below niche libraries.

title: Software Engineer
blurb: Engineering ATS filters key on languages, frameworks, and cloud platforms, so match the posting's exact stack names. Human reviewers then look for scale, ownership, and impact.
certs: Bachelor's in Computer Science or equivalent
bullets: Re-architected the checkout service into Go microservices, cutting p95 latency from 900ms to 180ms at 5K requests/sec.
Built CI/CD pipelines in GitHub Actions that took deploys from weekly to 20+ per day with zero-downtime rollbacks.
Led a React and TypeScript migration of a 200K-line codebase, cutting front-end bugs 40%.
mistakes: A skills list of 40 technologies with no indication of depth.
Bullets describing tasks ("worked on APIs") instead of outcomes.
No numbers for scale: users, requests, data size, latency.

title: Product Manager
blurb: PM resumes are screened for ownership of outcomes, not features. ATS keywords cluster around roadmap, discovery, experimentation, and metrics, so name the frameworks and tools the posting uses.
bullets: Owned the onboarding roadmap for a 3M-user app; shipped 4 experiments that lifted Week-1 activation from 31% to 44%.
Ran 50+ customer interviews to define a self-serve tier that added $2.4M ARR in its first two quarters.
Aligned engineering, design, and sales on a pricing change that raised ARPU 18% with no rise in churn.
mistakes: Listing features you shipped without the metric they moved.
Using "helped" or "supported" for work you owned.
No evidence of working with engineering and design.

title: Project Manager
blurb: Project manager screens look for methodology (Agile, Waterfall, PMP), budget and scope ownership, and on-time delivery. Name the size of what you ran: budget, team, timeline.
bullets: Delivered a $3.2M ERP rollout across 4 sites two weeks early and 6% under budget, coordinating 35 stakeholders.
Introduced Agile ceremonies to a 12-person team, raising on-time sprint completion from 58% to 91%.
Built a risk register and vendor scorecard that cut change-order costs 22% year over year.
mistakes: Listing duties without budget, team size, or timeline.
Missing the methodology named in the posting.
No proof of delivering on time or under budget.

title: Marketing Manager
blurb: Marketing manager screens blend channel expertise with business results. Expect the ATS to look for campaign strategy, budget ownership, and the platforms you run.
bullets: Owned a $1.8M annual budget across paid, email, and events; grew marketing-sourced pipeline 64% at a 4.1x ROI.
Launched an SEO content program that grew organic traffic from 20K to 110K monthly visits in 12 months.
Built HubSpot nurture streams that raised MQL-to-SQL conversion from 9% to 17%.
mistakes: Vanity metrics (impressions) with no link to pipeline or revenue.
No budget figure, which signals junior scope.
Generic "managed social media" bullets.

title: Digital Marketing Specialist
blurb: Digital marketing roles are tool-heavy and ATS filters reflect that. Name each ad platform and analytics tool you have run campaigns in, and pair them with spend and performance.
bullets: Managed $40K/month in Google and Meta ads, raising ROAS from 2.1x to 3.6x through audience and creative testing.
Rebuilt 12 landing pages with A/B tests that lifted conversion rate from 2.8% to 4.5%.
Grew the email list 3x to 85K subscribers with lead magnets and a 5-email welcome series.
mistakes: Listing platforms without spend levels.
No conversion or ROAS numbers.
Leaving out GA4 and Tag Manager, which many postings filter on.

title: Lifecycle Marketing Manager
blurb: Lifecycle and CRM roles are screened on your messaging platform (Braze, Iterable, Klaviyo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud), segmentation skill, and retention results. The platform name is often a hard filter.
bullets: Built a 7-touch onboarding journey in Braze that lifted Day-30 retention 14% across 1.2M new users.
Launched a win-back program with SQL-driven churn segments that recovered $680K in annual revenue.
Ran 60+ A/B tests on email and push cadence, raising LTV 11% while cutting unsubscribes 20%.
mistakes: Naming no messaging platform, which can fail a hard filter.
Reporting opens and clicks instead of retention and revenue.
No mention of segmentation or experimentation.

title: Growth Marketing Manager
blurb: Growth roles reward a full-funnel, experiment-driven story. ATS keywords cluster around acquisition, activation, retention, experimentation, and attribution, plus the analytics stack.
bullets: Cut blended CAC 28% in two quarters by shifting spend to high-LTV channels identified through attribution analysis.
Launched a referral program that drove 19% of new signups at one-third the CAC of paid.
Ran a 40-test experimentation roadmap across the funnel, compounding to a 33% lift in signup-to-paid conversion.
mistakes: Channel bullets with no funnel metric.
Missing CAC and LTV, the two numbers growth leaders scan for.
No sign of an experimentation process.

title: Product Marketing Manager
blurb: PMM resumes are screened for positioning, launches, and sales enablement. Show you can turn product capability into messaging that moves win rates and adoption.
bullets: Led positioning and launch for a new analytics product that hit 140% of its first-quarter pipeline target.
Built competitive battlecards from 80 Gong calls, raising head-to-head win rate from 32% to 46%.
Ran pricing research with 300 customers that informed a packaging change worth $3M in new ARR.
mistakes: Describing launches without adoption or pipeline results.
No sales enablement evidence.
Leaving out customer research methods.

title: Account Executive
blurb: Sales resumes are skimmed for quota attainment in seconds. Put percent of quota, deal size, and sales cycle in the first bullet of every role, and name the CRM and methodology.
bullets: Closed $1.9M in new ARR at 132% of quota, ranking #2 of 24 AEs; average deal size $85K.
Built 60% of own pipeline through outbound with Sales Navigator and Outreach sequences.
Shortened the enterprise sales cycle from 110 to 75 days by introducing MEDDICC-based mutual action plans.
mistakes: No quota attainment number, which recruiters read as a miss.
No deal size or segment (SMB, mid-market, enterprise).
Listing responsibilities instead of rankings and results.

title: Customer Success Manager
blurb: CSM screens focus on retention, expansion, and the size of the book you manage. Name your book value, renewal rate, and the CS platform you use.
bullets: Managed a $4.2M book of 45 mid-market accounts with a 96% gross renewal rate and 118% net revenue retention.
Rebuilt onboarding playbooks that cut time-to-value from 45 to 21 days.
Built Gainsight health scores that flagged at-risk accounts 60 days earlier, saving $500K in renewals.
mistakes: No book size or account count.
Missing renewal or NRR figures.
Describing support tickets instead of strategic outcomes.

title: Business Analyst
blurb: Business analyst postings filter on requirements gathering, process mapping, and SQL or BI tools. Show the bridge you built between stakeholders and delivery teams.
bullets: Gathered requirements from 20 stakeholders and wrote 140 user stories for a claims platform delivered on schedule.
Mapped the order-to-cash process and removed 4 handoffs, cutting cycle time 35%.
Built Power BI dashboards that replaced 10 manual reports and saved the finance team 15 hours a week.
mistakes: No named methodology or documentation artifacts.
Missing SQL or BI tools when the posting lists them.
Bullets with no measurable process outcome.

title: Financial Analyst
blurb: Financial analyst screens look for modeling, FP&A, and Excel depth, plus the ERP or planning tools you have used. Quantify the size of the budgets and forecasts you owned.
bullets: Built a driver-based forecast model for a $120M P&L that cut forecast variance from 8% to 2.5%.
Led monthly variance analysis for 6 business units, surfacing $1.4M in cost savings.
Automated the close package in Excel and Power BI, cutting reporting time from 5 days to 2.
mistakes: No size of budgets or P&Ls.
Generic "prepared reports" bullets.
Leaving out Excel modeling depth (Power Query, macros, scenario models).

title: Accountant
blurb: Accounting ATS filters look for GAAP, close, reconciliation, and your ERP. Licenses like CPA are often hard filters, so state them exactly as the posting does.
bullets: Cut month-end close from 10 days to 6 by standardizing reconciliations in BlackLine.
Managed AP for 600 vendors and $45M annual spend with zero audit findings two years running.
Documented SOX controls for revenue and payables, supporting a clean first-year audit.
mistakes: Omitting the ERP name, often a hard filter.
No close timeline or volume.
Writing "CPA eligible" vaguely instead of exam status.

title: UX Designer
blurb: Design resumes still pass through an ATS before a portfolio review. Name your research methods, design tools, and the product metrics your work moved, and link the portfolio in plain text.
bullets: Redesigned the checkout flow after 15 usability tests, raising completion from 61% to 78%.
Built a Figma design system of 120 components adopted by 4 product teams, cutting design-to-dev time 30%.
Led an accessibility audit and fixes that brought the app to WCAG 2.1 AA.
mistakes: No portfolio link in plain text.
Describing screens instead of user and business outcomes.
Putting the resume in a graphic layout that an ATS cannot parse.

title: Recruiter
blurb: Recruiter resumes are judged on hiring volume, time-to-fill, and the roles you specialize in. Name your ATS and sourcing tools, since hiring teams filter on them.
bullets: Hired 48 engineers in 12 months across 6 teams with a 34-day average time-to-fill against a 50-day benchmark.
Built Boolean and Gem sourcing campaigns that raised outbound response rate from 12% to 31%.
Partnered with 15 hiring managers to redesign interview loops, lifting offer acceptance from 72% to 89%.
mistakes: No hiring volume or time-to-fill.
Leaving out role types and seniority you recruit for.
Missing the ATS name.

title: Operations Manager
blurb: Operations screens look for process improvement, team leadership, and cost or efficiency results. State the size of the team, budget, and operation you ran.
bullets: Led a 35-person fulfillment team and raised on-time shipping from 88% to 98% while cutting overtime 25%.
Renegotiated 6 vendor contracts for $640K in annual savings.
Wrote 40 SOPs and a KPI dashboard that cut onboarding time for new hires from 4 weeks to 2.
mistakes: No team size or budget.
Process bullets with no efficiency number.
Missing the methodology (Lean, Six Sigma) named in the posting.

title: Registered Nurse
blurb: Nursing ATS filters key on license, certifications, unit type, and EHR system. Put your RN license and certifications near the top, exactly as the posting names them.
bullets: Provided care for 5 to 6 telemetry patients per shift on a 32-bed cardiac unit.
Led a fall-prevention initiative that cut unit falls 40% over 6 months.
Precepted 8 new graduate nurses with a 100% one-year retention rate.
mistakes: License and certifications buried at the bottom.
No unit type, bed count, or patient ratio.
Missing the EHR system named in the posting.

title: Administrative Assistant
blurb: Administrative postings filter on office software, scheduling, and communication skills. Quantify how many people, calendars, or events you supported.
bullets: Managed calendars and travel for 4 executives, coordinating 60+ meetings a week across 3 time zones.
Rebuilt the expense process in Concur, cutting reimbursement time from 3 weeks to 5 days.
Planned 12 company events a year for up to 200 attendees, finishing 10% under budget.
mistakes: Duties with no volume or scope.
Skipping software proficiency.
Generic soft-skill claims with no evidence.

title: Sales Development Representative
blurb: SDR screens are about activity and conversion: meetings booked, pipeline sourced, and the outbound stack you used. Quantify everything per month or quarter.
bullets: Booked 18 qualified meetings a month at 140% of target, sourcing $1.1M in pipeline in 2025.
Built a 6-step Outreach sequence with a 14% reply rate, double the team average.
Ranked #1 of 12 SDRs for two straight quarters and was promoted to AE in 14 months.
mistakes: No monthly meeting or pipeline numbers.
Leaving out the tools you prospected with.
Listing 'cold calling' without volume or conversion.

title: Customer Service Representative
blurb: Support resumes are screened for volume, satisfaction scores, and the helpdesk tools you know. Give numbers for tickets, CSAT, and response times.
bullets: Resolved 70+ tickets a day across chat, phone, and email with a 96% CSAT score.
Cut average first response time from 4 hours to 45 minutes by building 30 macros.
Wrote 25 help center articles that reduced repeat tickets on billing questions 18%.
mistakes: No ticket volume or CSAT numbers.
Missing the helpdesk software name.
Generic 'helped customers' bullets.

title: Executive Assistant
blurb: Executive assistant screens focus on scope: how senior the executives were, how many you supported, and how complex the calendars, travel, and projects were.
bullets: Supported the CEO and 2 SVPs of a 600-person company, managing 50+ meetings a week across 4 time zones.
Planned quarterly board meetings and an 80-person offsite on time and 12% under budget.
Built an Asana system for executive follow-ups that cut missed action items to zero over two quarters.
mistakes: No title or seniority of the executives supported.
Leaving out volume and complexity.
No proof of discretion or judgment.

title: Content Marketing Manager
blurb: Content roles are screened for strategy plus results: traffic, rankings, leads, and the publishing cadence you ran. Show the business outcome of content, not just the pieces.
bullets: Built a content program from zero to 120K monthly organic visits in 14 months, sourcing 30% of inbound demos.
Ran an editorial calendar of 12 posts a month with 5 freelance writers, on time every month.
Launched a quarterly research report that earned 90 backlinks and 1,400 leads.
mistakes: Counting posts instead of results.
No traffic, ranking, or lead numbers.
Leaving out SEO tools.

title: Social Media Manager
blurb: Social roles are screened for platform expertise, growth, engagement, and business results. Name each platform and the numbers you moved on it.
bullets: Grew TikTok from 0 to 85K followers in 9 months; 3 videos passed 1M views.
Raised Instagram engagement rate from 1.2% to 4.8% with a new Reels-first content mix.
Managed $25K a month in Meta ads at a 3.2x ROAS.
mistakes: Follower counts with no time frame.
No link from social to traffic or sales.
Missing the scheduling and analytics tools.

title: SEO Specialist
blurb: SEO screens look for technical depth, content strategy, and ranking and traffic results. Name your tools and the size of sites you worked on.
bullets: Grew organic traffic 210% in 12 months for a 4,000-page e-commerce site through a technical audit and internal linking.
Took 45 target keywords from page 3 to the top 5, adding $380K in organic revenue.
Fixed Core Web Vitals across 1,200 templates, passing all three metrics for the first time.
mistakes: No traffic or revenue results.
Missing technical SEO tools.
No site size or industry context.

title: Data Engineer
blurb: Data engineering screens key on pipeline tools, warehouses, and scale. Name the stack exactly and quantify data volume, latency, and reliability.
bullets: Built Airflow and dbt pipelines processing 2TB a day into Snowflake with 99.9% on-time delivery.
Migrated 140 legacy ETL jobs to Spark, cutting compute cost 38% and runtime from 6 hours to 50 minutes.
Added data quality tests that caught 95% of upstream schema breaks before they hit dashboards.
mistakes: No data volume or latency numbers.
Tool lists with no architecture context.
Missing reliability or cost results.

title: DevOps Engineer
blurb: DevOps and SRE screens look for cloud, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, and reliability metrics. Show uptime, deploy frequency, and cost results.
bullets: Moved 60 services to Kubernetes on EKS with Terraform, raising deploy frequency from weekly to 30+ a day.
Cut AWS spend 31% ($420K a year) with rightsizing, spot instances, and autoscaling.
Built Prometheus and Grafana alerting that cut mean time to recovery from 2 hours to 18 minutes.
mistakes: No uptime, MTTR, or deploy metrics.
Missing the cloud provider named in the posting.
Listing tools without scale.

title: Frontend Developer
blurb: Frontend screens match on framework, language, and tooling, then look for performance, accessibility, and product impact.
certs: Bachelor's in Computer Science or equivalent
bullets: Rebuilt the checkout in React and TypeScript, cutting load time 45% and lifting conversion 6%.
Built a component library of 80 accessible components used across 5 product teams.
Raised Lighthouse performance from 52 to 94 on the marketing site with code splitting and image optimization.
mistakes: No performance or business numbers.
Missing the framework named in the posting.
No portfolio or GitHub link.

title: Product Designer
blurb: Product design resumes are screened for end-to-end ownership, research, systems thinking, and measurable product outcomes, plus a portfolio link.
bullets: Led design of a new onboarding flow from research to launch, lifting activation 22%.
Built and maintained a Figma design system of 150 components used by 30 engineers.
Ran 40 usability sessions that reshaped the roadmap for a $5M ARR product line.
mistakes: No portfolio link.
Screens described without outcomes.
Missing research methods.

title: QA Engineer
blurb: QA screens look for automation frameworks, test strategy, and quality metrics. Show coverage, defect rates, and release speed.
bullets: Built a Playwright suite of 900 end-to-end tests running in CI, cutting regression time from 3 days to 40 minutes.
Reduced escaped production defects 60% in two quarters by adding API contract tests.
Raised automated coverage of critical flows from 35% to 92%.
mistakes: No coverage or defect numbers.
Missing the automation framework.
Only manual testing listed for automation roles.

title: IT Support Specialist
blurb: IT support resumes are screened for systems, ticket volume, and certifications. Name the operating systems, tools, and environments you supported.
bullets: Resolved 40+ tickets a day for 500 employees with a 98% satisfaction score.
Automated laptop provisioning with Intune, cutting new-hire setup from 4 hours to 30 minutes.
Rolled out Okta SSO to 30 apps with zero downtime.
mistakes: No ticket volume or user count.
Missing certifications.
Leaving out device management tools.

title: Cybersecurity Analyst
blurb: Security screens filter heavily on certifications, tools, and frameworks. Show incidents handled, vulnerabilities closed, and compliance work.
bullets: Triaged 300+ SIEM alerts a week in Splunk and cut false positives 45% by tuning detection rules.
Led response for 12 security incidents with no data loss and a 2-hour average containment time.
Drove remediation of 1,800 critical vulnerabilities to meet a SOC 2 audit deadline.
mistakes: Certifications buried at the bottom.
No incident or vulnerability numbers.
Missing frameworks (NIST, SOC 2, ISO 27001).

title: HR Generalist
blurb: HR generalist screens look for breadth across employee relations, benefits, onboarding, and compliance, plus the HRIS you have run.
bullets: Supported 350 employees across 3 states as the sole HR generalist, handling relations, benefits, and compliance.
Rebuilt onboarding in BambooHR, raising 90-day retention from 81% to 93%.
Led open enrollment for 400 employees with a 99% completion rate.
mistakes: No employee count or scope.
Missing the HRIS name.
No compliance or policy examples.

title: Supply Chain Analyst
blurb: Supply chain screens look for forecasting, inventory, and ERP skills, plus cost and service-level results.
bullets: Built a SKU-level demand forecast that cut forecast error from 32% to 18% across 1,400 SKUs.
Reduced excess inventory $2.3M while holding a 97% fill rate.
Automated weekly supply reports in Power BI, saving 10 hours a week.
mistakes: No inventory, cost, or service-level numbers.
Missing the ERP.
Generic 'analyzed data' bullets.

title: Teacher
blurb: Teaching resumes still pass through school district ATS systems. Lead with certification, grade levels, subjects, and student outcomes.
bullets: Raised the share of students meeting grade-level reading benchmarks from 54% to 78% in one year.
Taught 5 sections of 8th-grade math (130 students) using differentiated small-group instruction.
Built a project-based science unit adopted by 6 teachers across the district.
mistakes: Certification not near the top.
No student outcome data.
Missing grade levels and subjects.

title: Program Manager
blurb: Program manager screens look for cross-team scope, delivery of complex initiatives, and metrics. Show the number of teams, budget, and business result.
bullets: Led a 9-team, $6M platform migration delivered on schedule, retiring 3 legacy systems.
Built quarterly OKR and dependency planning across 14 teams, cutting blocked work 35%.
Ran weekly executive reviews for the CTO that surfaced risks an average of 3 weeks earlier.
mistakes: No team count or budget.
Describing meetings instead of outcomes.
Missing methodology from the posting.

title: Brand Manager
blurb: Brand management screens look for P&L ownership, campaign results, and consumer insight. Show market share, revenue, and the brands you managed.
bullets: Owned a $45M brand P&L and grew net sales 12% while holding margin.
Launched 3 new SKUs that reached $6M in first-year sales and 2 points of category share.
Led an integrated campaign with 2 agencies that lifted aided awareness from 31% to 44%.
mistakes: No P&L or revenue figures.
Missing consumer research methods.
Campaign bullets without business results.

title: Email Marketing Specialist
blurb: Email roles are screened on your ESP, segmentation, automation, and revenue results. The platform name is often a hard filter.
bullets: Built Klaviyo flows (welcome, browse, cart, post-purchase) that drove 32% of e-commerce revenue.
Raised inbox placement from 82% to 97% by fixing authentication and sunsetting inactive subscribers.
Ran 50 A/B tests a year, lifting click rate from 2.4% to 3.9%.
mistakes: Opens and clicks with no revenue.
Missing the ESP.
No deliverability work.

title: Revenue Operations Manager
blurb: RevOps screens look for CRM architecture, forecasting, and go-to-market process ownership across sales, marketing, and success.
bullets: Rebuilt Salesforce lead routing, cutting speed-to-lead from 9 hours to 12 minutes and lifting meeting rate 26%.
Built the forecast model the CRO used for board reporting, accurate within 4% for 6 quarters.
Designed territories and comp plans for a 60-rep team, raising quota attainment from 58% to 71%.
mistakes: No pipeline, forecast, or efficiency numbers.
Missing the CRM.
Admin tasks without business impact.
